source.stem: By which process does oxygen pass out of a leaf?

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: The tongue chews food into smaller pieces, and the teeth mix it with saliva.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: Chewing alone prepares food for swallowing; saliva and the tongue are not needed.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: Saliva starts digesting every part of food in the mouth, not just starch.

mx.name: mechanism_conflation
mx.teacher_note: Teeth chemically digest starch by crushing food into smaller pieces.

intelligence.enrichment: Teeth crush and chew food into smaller pieces, saliva moistens it and begins starch digestion, and the tongue mixes food with saliva and pushes the softened food for swallowing. teeth break food mechanically + saliva moistens and digests starch + tongue mixes and pushes -> softened food can be swallowed The learner correctly applies this rule: Teeth crush and chew food into smaller pieces, saliva moistens it and begins starch digestion, and the tongue mixes food with saliva and pushes the softened food for swallowing. The mouth only chews food; saliva and tongue do not change whether food can be swallowed.
